sectionTitle: Morality, Hiddenness, and the Evidential Force of Evil

lockedMove.speaker: William Lane Craig
lockedMove.excerpt: argument now notice what Dr Stinger did here was to redefine what is meant by objective he says objective means most people agree with it that's not what objective is that's iter subjective uh and I'm talking about whether or not moral values are objective in the sense that they hold and are binding regardless of whether anybody believes in them or not and I think Dr Stinger agrees with me that in the absence of God moral values are not objective in that sense and that's what the evolution of morality demonstrates and is all about so what I want to know is why is
lockedMove.proposition: Stenger substitutes intersubjective agreement for mind-independent obligation, leaving naturalistic moral conventions without objective validity.
